question.text:
A network administrator needs to create a single, efficient summary route that advertises a block of networks to a neighboring router. The summary route must precisely cover the following four network addresses and no more.

  • $192.168 .16 .0 / 24$
     
  • $192.168.17.0/24$
     
  • $192.168.18.0/24$
     
  • $192.168.19.0/24$

Which of the following represents the most efficient summary route for these networks?

  1. $192,168,16,0 / 23$
     
  2. $192.168 .19 .0 / 22$
     
  3. $192.168 .16 .0 / 22$
     
  4. $192.168.0.0 / 16$

question.text:
A server ($S$) and a workstation ($W$) are configured on a network as follows:

  • Server S has the IP address $172.16.70.20$ and the netmask $255.255.240.0$.
     
  • Workstation W has the IP address $172.16.10.100$ and the netmask $255.255.0.0$.

Which one of the following statements is true?

  1. $S$ and $W$ both assume they are on the same network.
     
  2. $S$ assumes $W$ is on the same network, but $W$ assumes $S$ is on a different network.
     
  3. $S$ assumes $W$ is on a different network, but $W$ assumes $S$ is on the same network.
     
  4. $S$ and $W$ both assume they are on different networks.

question.text:
The routing table of a corporate router is shown below:

\[
\begin{array}{l l l}
\textbf{Destination} & \textbf{Subnet Mask} & \textbf{Interface} \\
203.0.113.0 & 255.255.255.0 & \text{igb0} \\
203.0.113.128 & 255.255.255.192 & \text{igb1} \\
10.10.20.0 & 255.255.255.0 & \text{em0} \\
\text{Default} &  & \text{em1} \\
\end{array}
\]

On which interface will the router forward packets addressed to the destinations $203.0.113.140$ and $10.10 .30 .55$ , respectively?

  1. igb1 and em1
     
  2. igb0 and em1
     
  3. igb1 and em0
     
  4. igb0 and em0

question.text:
Host $X$ uses $64$ -byte packets to send data to Host $Y$ via a sliding window protocol. The round trip time (RTT) between X and Y is measured to be $100$ milliseconds, and the bottleneck bandwidth of the path is $512$ kbps . To achieve maximum throughput, what is the optimal window size (in packets) that Host $X$ should configure?

  1. $50$
     
  2. $100$
     
  3. $200$
     
  4. $800$
question.subject: Computer Networks

question.text:
Server S is transmitting data to client C over a full-duplex connection. S and C use the sliding window protocol for flow control. The send and receive window sizes are $8$ packets each. Data packets (sent from S to C) are $1500$ bytes long, and the connection's bandwidth is $200$ Mbps. Acknowledgement packets (sent from C to S ) are very small and have a negligible transmission time. The propagation delay for the connection is $270 \mu \mathrm{~s}$. What is the maximum possible throughput for this data transmission?

  1. $125.50 \times 10^6 \mathrm{Bps}$
     
  2. $160.00 \times 10^6 \mathrm{Bps}$
     
  3. $177.78 \times 10^6 \mathrm{Bps}$
     
  4. $200.00 \times 10^6 \mathrm{Bps}$
